This API manages the Unity Catalog securables that bring centralized access control, lineage, and auditing to AI-serving entities: model services (governed access to foundation models and external LLMs), model provider services (governed resources for external model providers), and MCP services (governed Model Context Protocol servers).

An index has a primary key and an index type (`DELTA_SYNC`, which keeps the index in sync with a source Delta table, or `DIRECT_ACCESS`, which is written to directly through the API). Indexes are immutable once created. This resource is the AIP-conformant replacement for the legacy `databricks_vector_search_index` resource and is functionally equivalent.

evidence.quote: UniForm takes advantage of the fact that Delta Lake, Iceberg, and Hudi all consist of Parquet data files and a metadata layer. UniForm automatically generates Iceberg metadata asynchronously, allowing Iceberg clients to read Delta tables as if they were Iceberg or Hudi tables.

Delta Lake triggers Iceberg/Hudi metadata generation asynchronously after a Delta Lake write transaction completes using the same compute that completed the Delta transaction. ... Delta tables with frequent commits might bundle multiple Delta commits into a single Iceberg/Hudi commit. ... Commits that would trigger a second concurrent metadata generation process successfully commit to Delta, but do not trigger asynchronous metadata generation.

Temporary Table Credentials are short-lived, downscoped credentials used to access cloud storage locations where table data is stored in Databricks. ... AWS uses temporary session tokens through AWS Security Token Service (STS), Azure uses Shared Access Signatures (SAS) for its data storage services, and Google Cloud supports temporary credentials through OAuth 2.0. ... To use the temporary table credentials API, a metastore admin must enable the external_access_enabled flag (off by default) at the metastore level, and the user must be granted the EXTERNAL USE SCHEMA permission at the schema level by the catalog owner. Note that EXTERNAL USE SCHEMA is a schema level permission that can only be granted by the catalog owner explicitly and is not included in schema ownership or ALL PRIVILEGES on the schema for security reasons.

claims.finding: Contradiction confirmed by my own re-read of the SDK at the v2.2.0 tag, and the first correction's overreach fixed after the adversarial review. AuthSettings.validate_token_resource defaults to None; with resource_server_url set but the flag unset the SDK warns and behaves as False; both the low-level server and MCPServer pass resource_server_url to BearerAuthBackend only when the flag is truthy, so the SDK's own resource comparison is opt-in. But BearerAuthBackend.authenticate returns None, which becomes 401 invalid_token, whenever the configured TokenVerifier returns None, and TokenVerifier.verify_token's docstring says that without the flag, confirming the token was issued for this server is up to the verifier. So the first correction's handbook sentence ("refused with 401 only when validate_token_resource is set to True: left unset, 2.2.0 warns") went too far twice: a verifier that checks the audience also refuses, and the warning fires only with resource_server_url set. Executed in this build (mcp 2.2.0 wheel from PyPI, the five auth files byte-identical to tag v2.2.0; MCPServer.streamable_http_app with a Starlette TestClient, POST /mcp): with resource_server_url set, a token issued for another resource got 200 when neither validate_token_resource nor the verifier checked the audience (setting unset or False), and 401 when either did (setting True, or a verifier that returns None for another audience with the setting unset or False); the missing token got 401 and the token without the required scope 403 in every case; the MCPDeprecationWarning fired only with the setting unset and resource_server_url set, not without a resource server URL. As now taught every assertion is supported: 401 invalid_token for a missing, expired or verifier-rejected token, 403 insufficient_scope for the endpoint-wide required scopes (bearer_auth.py, low-level server), the SDK's own audience comparison only with validate_token_resource and otherwise the verifier's job (settings.py, provider.py), the warning only with a resource server URL (settings.py), protected resource metadata when a resource server URL is configured (routes.py), handlers reading the verified token (get_access_token), no per-tool authorization parameter on the tool decorator, OAuth for HTTP transports and credentials from the environment for stdio, the specification's audience requirement and no token passthrough (specification, authorization page). claims.finding: Over-promotion corrected. The course claim said, unconditionally, "urllib3 retries by default only methods considered idempotent, which excludes POST." urllib3 2.6.3's Retry.increment retries a connection error (ConnectTimeoutError, including NewConnectionError), raised before the request is sent, for any method; only read errors and status retries are gated by allowed_methods. Executed in this build with the urllib3 2.6.3 wheel (retry.py byte-identical to tag 2.6.3): under Retry(3) a POST to a closed local port raised MaxRetryError after 4 increment calls, reason NewConnectionError (a ConnectTimeoutError), exactly as a GET did; against a server that accepts but never replies, a POST raised ReadTimeoutError after 1 connection while a GET raised MaxRetryError after 4, and a POST with allowed_methods=None was retried like the GET. The claim now reads "urllib3 retries a read timeout by default only for methods considered idempotent, which excludes POST.", which the retry code and the run support. The lesson sentence, in the paragraph about a reply that did not arrive in time, now reads "urllib3 retries a late reply to a GET or PUT by default, not to a POST."
